column1: # catalog/ci-batch-escalate.tsv — which changed paths make a Mergify merge-queue
# batch run the WHOLE corpus instead of its impact set (BH-4968). Read by
# bin/lib/ci-batch-escalate.sh, which bin/ci-plan.sh asks once per changed path
#   pattern  ending in / : a prefix (bin/lib/ matches everything under bin/lib)
#            anything else: a bash glob matched against the whole path
#   kind     escalate | infra | allow. An allow row exempts a path an escalate
#            or infra row would catch. Rows of any other kind belong to another
#   why      one line, for the reviewer of this file
# KINDS spa AND worker (BH-4969) are read by cbe_affects, not cbe_reason (which
# skips them). On a batch that stays batch-selected, bin/ci-plan.sh writes
# spa=0 (worker=0) when no changed path is affected, and the console-ui
# (worker-jobs) job then runs only its "not affected by this batch" step. A
# path under console-ui/ (worker/) is always affected, row or no row; these rows
# add the paths OUTSIDE those trees each job builds or tests from: what
# console-ui/ and worker/jobs/ import or read by a relative path (a guard in
# tests/ci-plan-spa-worker.bh-4969-test.sh fails on one with no row here), and
# the scripts the jobs' own workflow steps run. A path that also escalates still
# carries its row, so deleting an escalate row cannot un-gate a job. Every
# non-batch-selected run, and an escalated batch, runs both jobs whole.
# A TOP-LEVEL WORKFLOW FILE (BH-6876) is an allow row: a batch that edits
# .github/workflows/<x>.yml or <x>.yaml runs the suites that read that file
# plus the always set (bin/test-impact.sh, TI_BATCH_SELECT=1), and the nightly
# corpus is the backstop. Every other .github/ path still escalates. An allow
# row beats a CI_FULL_TRIGGERS `+` row too: to escalate workflow edits again,
# remove the two allow rows by PR.
# THE ESCALATE ROWS are what still runs the whole corpus: a .github/ path that
# is not a top-level workflow, .mergify.yml, and this file when its diff
# deletes a row (see below). The file fails closed: unreadable, or no escalate
# INFRA ROWS (BH-7287, BH-7033.1) are the paths the selection itself runs on:
# the planner, the selector and tier step, the libs and catalogs those three
# source and read, the runners, and tests/lib/scratch.sh. A batch that touches
# one used to prove everything (2,487 suites). It now runs, mode=infra:
#   1. the self and reads suites of each infra path (bin/test-impact.sh select
#      --why --map-only), the suites that test that file;
#   2. the fixed canary list catalog/ci-infra-canary.txt, 40 suites over each
#      runner path (scratch sandbox, docker runner, suite runner, tiers, reuse
#      ledger); a list that cannot be read or checked runs the corpus;
#   3. the normal selection of the batch's other paths, always set included.
# An escalate row beats an infra row, so CI_FULL_TRIGGERS=+<path> forces one
# back to the corpus with no PR. The nightly corpus is the backstop.
# BH-6059 replaced the blanket `bin/lib/` and `catalog/` rows with the files
# below: 19 of 21 sampled batches ran the whole corpus through them, a README
# included. Every other bin/lib/ or catalog/ path runs its impact set, and one
# the impact map has no specific row for (a new file, a deleted one) still

# escalates, as `unmapped path

`: bin/test-impact.sh does that under
# TI_BATCH_SELECT=1, which only bin/ci-plan.sh's batch select sets. The rows
# are derived from what the scripts source and read; a guard in
# test-impact's infra list has no row here. Not rows, on purpose:
# catalog/ci-suite-durations.tsv (shard weights, not which suites run),
# never read when a batch is selected).
# BH-6371 replaced the blanket `tests/lib/` row the same way. A changed helper
# under tests/lib/ selects every suite that sources or imports it, directly or
# through another helper (bin/test-impact.sh's helper closure, again only under

# TI_BATCH_SELECT=1), and one that no suite reaches is `unmapped path

`. An
# infra row under tests/lib/ is the list of GLOBAL helpers: one whose change
# is a change to about every suite, so its impact set is the corpus anyway.
# A DIFF TO THIS FILE has three outcomes. bin/ci-plan.sh reads the batch's own
#   AN ADD-ONLY DIFF (BH-6371, cbe_add_only) selects through the map: every
#   changed line is an added line, at least one is a row, and every added row
#   is `pattern<TAB>kind<TAB>why` with kind escalate, spa or worker. An added
#   spa (worker) row turns that job on.
#   A DELETE (BH-7287, cbe_deletes_row) escalates: a removed row whose
#   `pattern<TAB>kind` is not added back (a kind change included), an added
#   allow row, a malformed row, an empty diff or one that cannot be read.
#   ANY OTHER DIFF (a why edit, a comment edit, a moved row, an added infra
#   row) is an infra path: its own suites plus the canaries.
# The allow rows exempt docs: a *.md never escalates on its own.
